capture.final_message:
Split the outer conjunction.

- For the first component, compare \(n\) and \(q\). If \(n<q\), apply \(H\). Otherwise \(q\le n\), and use the given prime \(p\): one has \(n<p\) by `hn`, while
  \[
  p\le 2q\le 2n
  \]
  by `covering`.

- For the second component, prove both universally quantified statements independently, then form the equivalence since both are true. The left statement is the standard compatibility of primality for a natural numeral viewed in \(\mathbb Z\), reducing integer primality to `Nat.Prime` via nonnegativity/natural absolute value. The right statement is the lying-over theorem for faithfully flat algebra extensions: the induced map on prime spectra is surjective, so every prime ideal \(p\subseteq A\) has a prime ideal \(P\subseteq B\) lying over it.

Thus the main mechanisms are a two-case order argument for the prime interval and the standard “faithfully flat implies surjective on spectra” result.
